en.title: Relative pronouns
en.summary: A relative pronoun begins a clause that adds information about a noun.

paragraphs: A relative pronoun joins a clause to a noun and refers back to it. The main ones are who, whom, whose, which and that. The noun it refers to is called the antecedent.

items: The woman **who** lives next door is a doctor.
The book **that** I bought was expensive.
The man **whose** car was stolen called the police.

blocks.html:
PronounRefers toExample
whopeopleThe girl who won is my cousin.
whompeople (object, formal)The man whom I met was kind.
whichthings and animalsThe car which broke down is old.
thatpeople or things (defining)The film that we saw was long.
whosepossessionThe woman whose bag was lost

paragraphs: You can leave out who, which or that when it is the object of the clause: The book I bought was expensive. You cannot leave it out when it is the subject: The man who called is here.
A defining clause identifies which person or thing you mean, and has no commas. A non-defining clause adds extra information, is separated by commas, and cannot use that.

blocks.html:
DefiningNon-defining
The student who works hard succeeds.My brother, who lives in Leeds, works hard.
The house that I like is old.This house, which is old, is for sale.

paragraphs: A preposition can stay at the end (informal) or move before the pronoun (formal): The man I spoke to; the man to whom I spoke.

items: Wrong: **The man which called is here.** Right: **who called**
Wrong: **My sister, that lives in Rome, is a nurse.** Right: **My sister, who lives in Rome**
Wrong: **The book that I read it was good.** Right: **The book that I read was good.** (do not repeat the object)
